names_flaws.span: A single photo can’t see what’s behind the first row.
AI is bad at gauging volume and freshness from a single image.
You’d need to expand the photo-scanning to the entire kitchen, which is a huge request for a first-time user.
This is a wildly complex constraint-satisfaction problem.
An LLM can generate a list of recipes, but its suggestions can be bizarre (“Make a spinach-yogurt-chicken smoothie!”) or require unnoticed pantry staples.
Curation and reliability are paramount; one bad recipe demolishes trust.
The app becomes a chore itself.
The fantasy of the all-seeing AI that manages your kitchen from a single snapshot is currently a trap that will lead to a poor user experience.
